title: Finding
description: A finding emitted by the engine for one rule against one source location.

fixes.description:
Byte-precise fixes resolving the finding; absent on the wire when
empty, so payloads produced before this field existed remain valid.

location.description: Source location where the rule fired.

rule-id.description: Identifier of the rule that produced this finding.

severity.description: Effective severity for this finding (may be overridden by user config).

trace.description:
Machine-readable derivation trace; absent on the wire when empty, so
payloads produced before this field existed remain valid.

Applicability.description: How safely a [`Fix`] can be applied without human review.

oneOf.description: The fix is proven correct; an automated applier may apply it.
The fix expresses intent but needs human review before applying.

Fix.description:
One byte-precise replacement that resolves (part of) a [`Finding`].

A fix replaces exactly the bytes of `range` in the finding's file with
`replacement`. Multi-edit fixes carry several entries; appliers must
apply entries of one finding together or not at all.

applicability.description: How safely the fix can be applied automatically.

range.description: Byte range in the finding's file that the replacement covers.

Range.description: Half-open byte range within a file.

Severity.description: Severity of a rule or a finding.

oneOf.description: Non-blocking concern that should be addressed.

TraceStep.description:
One step of the machine-readable derivation trace of a [`Finding`].

A step pairs an observed fact (what the engine saw in the analyzed
sources) with the reason that fact contributes to the finding. The
ordered step list reconstructs how the finding was derived without
parsing the human-readable message.

fact.description: Observed evidence, e.g. an offending item with its file.

reason.description: Why the fact contributes to the finding.
